about: Single source for /dev-kit:help and the generated docs (docs/skills.md, docs/recipes.md, docs/glossary.md). English only; the help skill answers in the user's language. Edit here, then run: python3 -I skills/core/scripts/dev_docs.py build

categories.title: Bugs, changes and what is pending

skills.name: start
skills.one_line: Entry point: starts a new project, adopts an existing codebase (feature, maintenance or import mode) or resumes, and routes to the next skill.
skills.when: First command in any project, and whenever you come back and want to know where things stopped.

args.meaning: a project idea starts the interview; in an existing codebase it is the goal of the change, after the onboarding (baseline tag, discovery, test baseline)
resume: reconcile with git and route

examples.what: new project: git init if needed, then the interview

examples.command: /dev-kit:start add CSV export to the reports page
examples.what: existing codebase without .dev/: onboarding (baseline tag, discovery, test baseline, retroactive ADRs), then a short interview about the change

skills.produces: routing only; starts a session in the log

skills.name: help
skills.one_line: Help inside Claude Code: what to do next, how each skill works, recipes and concepts.
skills.when: Whenever you are unsure which skill to use or what something means.

args.meaning: next steps for this project and the skill map
the recipe or concept that answers it
the agents and who calls them
a term such as gate, buffer or baseline: its definition

examples.what: how to report bugs and improvements

examples.command: /dev-kit:help how do I run it overnight?

skills.name: interview
skills.one_line: Exhaustive requirements interview in 10 blocks; everything goes to .dev/brief.md with the autonomy policy.
skills.when: Beginning of a project (start calls it), or later to answer questions the kit parked.

args.meaning: one round with the 4 most important questions

examples.what: resolve what the kit parked or assumed

skills.name: status
skills.one_line: Read-only dashboard: phase, milestones, gates, scores, issues, preview, production drift, cost so far.
skills.when: Any time you want a quick picture of the project.

skills.name: board
skills.one_line: Live Scrum board in the browser: what needs you, what is running now, the sprint kanban with live agents and task details, burndown, velocity, quality and backlog; light or dark; local, or shared on your network with an access link.
skills.when: When you want to watch the project visually, e.g. while implement or autopilot works; it updates by itself.

args.meaning: start the local server (or reuse the running one) and open the default browser
stop the server (the page also has a Stop server button)
whether it is running, its URL and PID
force a new tab, do not open a tab, preferred port (default 8765)
listen address (default 127.0.0.1); 0.0.0.0 shares the board on the network, opened only with the access link it prints
stop after N minutes with no open tab (default 120; 0 = never)

examples.what: open the board; calling it again does not start a second server or a second tab
share it on your network (phone, another computer) with a private access link

skills.produces: nothing in the project (read-only); its own files in .dev/run/

skills.name: prd
skills.one_line: Product requirements with user stories and numbered acceptance criteria (AC-n).
skills.when: After the interview, or to revise requirements when scope changes.

examples.what: write the PRD from the brief

skills.name: architecture
skills.one_line: Stack, repository layout, data model, contracts, environments, deploy commands and ADRs.
skills.when: After the PRD passes review, or when a structural decision must be revisited.

skills.name: ux
skills.one_line: Information architecture, journeys, every screen state, forms and microcopy guide.
skills.when: Products with a UI, after architecture, or to redesign a flow.

skills.name: ui
skills.one_line: Design tokens, components with states, and a spec for every screen (responsive, dark mode, accessibility).
skills.when: After ux, or to (re)specify a screen or component.

skills.name: plan
skills.one_line: Milestones M1..Mn and small vertical-slice tasks T-xxx with dependencies, ACs and files.
skills.when: After design (or architecture for UI-less products), and to replan remaining work.

args.meaning: rewrite only todo tasks of future milestones

skills.name: review
skills.one_line: Scored independent review (0-100, with cut-off) of the PRD, design, plan or docs, looping until it passes.
skills.when: Before implementation (prd, design, plan) and before release (docs).

examples.what: score the PRD and revise until it passes

skills.name: autopilot
skills.one_line: Drives the whole build on its own, from PRD to release; pauses follow your autonomy settings.
skills.when: After the interview, when you want the app built with minimal interaction (also overnight).

args.meaning: stop after a phase (e.g. plan to review documents first)
stop after N approved gates, to resume in a fresh session (cheaper long runs)

examples.what: only the documents, so you can review them
one milestone, e.g. to gauge cost
two milestones, then resume in a new session

skills.produces: everything below, one commit per task

skills.name: implement
skills.one_line: Implements ready tasks test-first, full suite, one commit per task; hotfix lane first.
skills.when: To build tasks by hand instead of autopilot, or to run a specific task (e.g. a fix).

args.meaning: N isolated implementers in git worktrees
work past a pending gate (records an ADR and sets the gate skipped)

skills.produces: code, tests, one commit per task

skills.name: test
skills.one_line: Test strategy and test writing: plan, missing tests for a task or path, flaky tests.
skills.when: Tests are missing, failing or flaky, or you want to define the testing approach.

args.meaning: cover a task or a folder

examples.what: add missing tests for a folder

skills.name: qa
skills.one_line: Milestone gate: auditors in parallel, 0-100 score per dimension, fix tasks until the cut-off is met.
skills.when: When a milestone's tasks are done, or to check one task (e.g. after a hotfix).

skills.name: usability
skills.one_line: Whole-product audit of usability, accessibility, visuals and copy, with score and fix tasks.
skills.when: After the UI milestones are built, before release.

skills.name: issue
skills.one_line: Report a bug, improvement or scope change in plain words; the kit classifies and routes it without breaking the milestone cadence.
skills.when: You found a bug or want something to work differently, during or after the build.

examples.command: /dev-kit:issue "the Save button on the profile page does nothing"

examples.what: turn a deferred finding into an issue

skills.name: backlog
skills.one_line: Everything pending: hotfix, issue queue, next buffer, tasks, parked questions, deferred findings, deploys.
skills.when: You want to know what is left or what to do next.

examples.what: the full list and the recommended next step

skills.name: deploy
skills.one_line: Production deploy of an approved milestone or release: preflight, backup, dry-run, install, migrations, smoke checks.
skills.when: After a gate when the project deploys per milestone, at release, or to check how far production is behind.

args.meaning: preflight and the method's own dry-run; nothing installed or recorded

skills.name: docs
skills.one_line: Project documentation from the artifacts and code: README, user guide, API reference, CHANGELOG.
skills.when: Before a release, or when you need docs for the project.

skills.name: release
skills.one_line: Release checklist and execution: audits, version, CHANGELOG, tag; patch releases for hotfixes.
skills.when: When the build is done and you want to ship, or after a hotfix.

args.meaning: patch release for a closed hotfix

examples.what: ship a hotfix as a patch version

skills.name: costs
skills.one_line: Token usage and estimated US$ (API-equivalent) per stage, agent, model or session; CSV of tokens.
skills.when: You want to know how much was spent and where.

examples.what: cost of this session by stage
whole project by agent, with CSV

skills.name: feedback
skills.one_line: Evaluation of the session: grade per stage with reasons, what worked and failed, suggestions for the kit.
skills.when: After a run, to review it or to send feedback to the dev-kit author.

recipes.title: Build a new app
steps: /dev-kit:start <your idea> and answer the interview
/dev-kit:autopilot --until plan, then read the PRD, design and plan
/dev-kit:autopilot to build the rest
/dev-kit:status at any time

recipes.title: Adopt dev-kit in an existing project
steps: Commit or stash pending work, then /dev-kit:start <the change you want> in the repository root
Onboarding: baseline tag dev-kit-baseline, .dev/discovery.md (stack, conventions, existing docs), test baseline, ADRs discovered/imported
Pick the entry mode: feature (new capability), maintenance (bugs only: straight to /dev-kit:issue) or import (use the project's PRD/specs/ADRs)
A stage was skipped? /dev-kit:start routes to the first missing artifact; a stage that does not apply is recorded as review n/a
QA scores only what changed since the baseline; pre-existing problems become intangible issues

recipes.title: Let it run overnight
steps: Choose 'unattended with floors' in the interview (or: dev_state.py set autonomy.level unattended)
Cover permission prompts: /fewer-permission-prompts and --permission-mode acceptEdits
Run inside tmux: claude --permission-mode acceptEdits "/dev-kit:autopilot"
In the morning: /dev-kit:status, /dev-kit:backlog, /dev-kit:costs, /dev-kit:interview --gaps

recipes.title: I found a bug
steps: /dev-kit:issue "what happens and where"
Confirm the class the kit proposes (hotfix, current, standard, intangible)
Hotfix: /dev-kit:implement T-xxx → /dev-kit:qa --scope T-xxx → /dev-kit:deploy → /dev-kit:release --hotfix
Otherwise it waits in the queue for the next milestone's buffer or the cool-down

recipes.title: I want an improvement
steps: /dev-kit:issue "what should be better"
Standard improvements enter the next milestone's buffer; small ones the cool-down
See the queue with /dev-kit:backlog issues

recipes.title: Change the scope (new feature, different behaviour)
steps: /dev-kit:issue "the new behaviour" (class change)
Accept the chain prd → review prd → (ux/ui → review design) → plan replan
The new tasks land in future milestones; the cadence does not change

recipes.title: What is left to do?
steps: /dev-kit:backlog for everything pending and the recommended next step
/dev-kit:status for the overall picture

recipes.title: How much did it cost?
steps: /dev-kit:costs for this session by stage
/dev-kit:costs --all --by agent for the whole project
/dev-kit:costs --csv to apply your own prices

recipes.title: Put it in production
steps: Answer the production questions in the interview (method, host, when, smoke checks, prerequisites)
/dev-kit:deploy --check to see the drift
/dev-kit:deploy M3 or let autopilot deploy per milestone

recipes.title: Resume after a crash or a reboot
steps: /dev-kit:start to reconcile state with git
/dev-kit:autopilot continues from the current phase
dev_state.py cleanup if processes were left behind

recipes.title: Review the session or send feedback to the author
steps: /dev-kit:feedback writes a graded report and an export without project data
Review both files in .dev/feedback/ before sending them

recipes.title: Change autonomy, quality or other settings
steps: /dev-kit:interview --gaps to revisit decisions
Or directly: dev_state.py set autonomy.<field> <value> (level, quality, cooldown, issue_buffer_pct, tips, model_policy, pause_policy…)

recipes.title: Watch the project on a board (or share it)
steps: /dev-kit:board opens the live board in the browser (one server per project)
/dev-kit:board --host 0.0.0.0 shares it on your network: open the access link it prints on the other device
/dev-kit:board stop (or the Stop server button) when done

recipes.title: Ship a version
steps: /dev-kit:docs all, then /dev-kit:review docs
/dev-kit:release --dry-run to see the checklist and the version it would use
/dev-kit:release (tags; pushes and deploys only as the brief allows)

recipes.title: Check that the app is usable and accessible
steps: /dev-kit:usability (or --url http://localhost:3000 for an app already running)
/dev-kit:implement to run the fix tasks it created
/dev-kit:usability again until review ux passes

glossary.definition: Acceptance criterion, numbered AC-n in the PRD; every task and test points to the ACs it satisfies.
Architecture decision record in .dev/decisions.md; source auto, user, interview, policy, discovered or imported.
A cadence step M1, M2…; the next one starts only after the previous gate passes. Issues never renumber milestones.
The quality check at the end of a milestone (qa): passes only with no critical/high findings and every score above its cut-off.
Minimum score for a gate or review, set in the interview (standard 85, premium 92, prototype 70).
From round 2, auditors verify whether previous findings were closed; new low findings are recorded but not scored.
Low findings cost at most 10 points per dimension.
How an issue is scheduled: expedite (hotfix), current, standard (buffer), intangible (cool-down) or change (replan).
Share of each milestone (default 20%) reserved for queued issues.
Optional short slot after a gate where small issues are fixed before the next milestone.
Expedite lane for critical/high bugs in delivered work: one at a time, scoped QA, patch release.
Priority lane of a task: hotfix runs first, then cool-down, then the plan.
Per-agent isolation number that gives each agent its own port, database and scratch folder.

Pause-point action: never wait; record the question with the recommended answer, block only what depends on it and continue (the default of most points under the unattended level, available at any level).
What the kit does at each pause point: ask, preauthorize within a limit, apply the recommendation, or park.
Agents start on their base model and effort; failed dimensions are re-run one step higher, with consent.
Estimated US$ of the tokens at API prices; on subscription plans nothing is billed per token.
.dev/telemetry.jsonl: structured, high-level events of the run, without project data.
The git tag dev-kit-baseline set by the onboarding: everything before it is legacy, everything after it is new work that QA scores.

An existing project not built with dev-kit. start runs the onboarding (baseline tag, discovery, test baseline, entry mode); audits score only the changes since the baseline and legacy problems become issues (conventions §16).
A finding in code that existed before dev-kit (existing projects): reported with "legacy": true, never scored, turned into an issue.
How an existing project is adopted: feature (new capability), maintenance (bugs and small improvements through issues) or import (existing PRD/specs are the source).
In maintenance mode, the milestone M<n> — Maintenance that issues fill; its gate runs like any other, then the next issue opens M<n+1>.
Tags of ACs and screens in existing projects: existing works already (no task), changed gets a task, new is built from scratch.
A review that does not apply (e.g. design with no new UI); recorded with a note, it satisfies prerequisites and is not graded.
The onboarding report of an existing project (.dev/discovery.md): stack, layout, commands, conventions, existing docs and ADRs.
production.method external: the project's own CI/CD deploys; the kit only confirms and records the commit.
The approved milestone built and run on 127.0.0.1 (keep_running or smoke), per autonomy.local_deploy.
A task removed by a replan (dev_state.py drop): kept for history, never counted by milestones, next or release.
The private URL printed by /dev-kit:board --host 0.0.0.0; other devices open the shared board only through it.
The class of service for a critical/high bug in delivered work: a hotfix task that runs before everything (WIP 1).
